packages.reason:
Torah #167 contains a single bechina equation: the Shabbatot spent with the true Talmid Chacham (the true tzaddik) ARE LIKE a fast (תַּעֲנִית). The language 'הֵם כְּמוֹ' declares essential identity of spiritual nature — not mere resemblance, but ontological equivalence at the level of their spiritual effect on the soul. Both nodes — שַׁבָּת אֵצֶל הַתַּלְמִיד-חָכָם and תַּעֲנִית — share the same essential quality: the suspension of the body's ordinary activity in order to elevate the soul. A fast (תַּעֲנִית) works by withdrawing the body from its regular nourishment, thereby redirecting energy from the physical to the spiritual, refining the soul and atoning for sin. Shabbat spent with the tzaddik works through an identical spiritual mechanism: the ordinary weekday self — its thoughts, its physicality, its everyday concerns — is 'fasted' from, while the soul feeds on the tzaddik's presence, Torah, and the holiness of Shabbat itself. The result is the same spiritual tikun as a fast, achieved through the opposite physical means (Shabbat is when one must eat and rejoice, yet it achieves what the fast achieves through restraint). This equivalence is the paradox that requires 'דַּע וְהַאֲמֵן' — knowledge and faith — because it is counterintuitive: the feast-day achieves what the fast-day achieves.

Both nodes belong entirely to the domain of holiness and positive spiritual practice (polarity: good). A fast is a holy practice for tikun and spiritual elevation. Shabbat is the holy seventh day. The tzaddik's presence transforms Shabbat into an intensified vehicle of the same spiritual work that fasting performs. There is no evil mirror in this Torah — no opposing force is named, no klipah is discussed, no negative counterpart is introduced. The Torah is a pure affirmation of the spiritual power of the tzaddik-Shabbat nexus.

The dominant node is תַּעֲנִית (fasting) rather than שַׁבָּת, because the teaching's rhetorical force is the revelation that Shabbat achieves what we ordinarily attribute exclusively to fasting — the fast is the known reference point that the Shabbat-tzaddik combination is declared equivalent to. The entire surprise of the Torah lies in the elevation of Shabbat-with-tzaddik to the status of תַּעֲנִית. However, the node שַׁבָּת אֵצֶל הַתַּלְמִיד-חָכָם הָאֱמֶת is the subject (the thing being elevated), so in a sense it is the operative concept the teaching wishes to promote.
